description.narrative: Lesotho - HEALTH SECTOR PROJECT - Health Care Centers Infrastructure Activity: This Project activity focuses on renovation and rehabilitation of up to 150 health centers, to bring the national stock of health centers up to a common standard. MCC Funding will support the following: (i) the design and construction supervision for up to 150 health centers; (ii) the rehabilitation and/or construction of these health centers; (iii) preparation of environmental "Project Briefs"; (iv) implementation of environmental and social mitigation measures; (v) power, water, telecommunications equipment as needed to reach MoHSW standards for these health centers; and (vi) medical equipment and instruments and clinical furniture as required to meet MoHSW clinic standards.
Capital of Lesotho, Maseru

condition.narrative: Adequate number and levels of Central Laboratory personnel included in MoHSW personnel -- positions established and fully funded.
Full compliance with the EMP and RAP or RPF (if necessary), and any requirements stipulated in the environmental license, for each MCC-funded facility.
Further details on conditions precedent affecting this activity can be found in the top-level parent activities.
Government to provide adequate funding for incremental recurrent costs for Compact activities.

Government will provide (1) evidence that a broad-based,�inter-ministerial working group is undertaking actions�to further effective management of health services at the decentralized level, including roles and responsibilities of the working group and minutes of monthly meetings for�at least three�months; and (2)�a plan, agreed cross-ministerially as appropriate,�detailing the role and functions of the central ministries and the local government structures, with clear lines of authority, fiscal responsibility, logistical management�and accountability for outcomes with regard to health services.
MCA-Lesotho has selected and engaged the Infrastructure Coordinator, approved by MCC, or in the event the position is vacant, MCA-Lesotho is actively recruiting for the position.

MCA-Lesotho will ensure that any project-specific Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA or EA), Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and/or Resettlement Action Plan or Framework (RAP or RPF) that is required to comply with MCC Environmental Guidelines, MCC Gender Policy, and World Bank Operational Policy on Involuntary Resettlement, OP 4.12, is prepared for each facility, or group of facilities, to the satisfaction of MCC.

MCA-Lesotho will have (1) developed an HIV/AIDS awareness program according to international best practice and to the satisfaction of MCC, (2) integrated the program into all construction contracts, and (3) established a mechanism acceptable to MCC for independent monitoring of the program for the life of the activity.

MCA-Lesotho will have all legal rights necessary for its contractors to perform the rehabilitation and related activities with respect to each health center that is part of the health centers activity.

MCA-Lesotho will have obtained and have on file all environmental and other licenses and permits as required by the National Environment Act of 2001 and any future amendments, validly issued and in full effect, necessary to perform each project activity.

The Government will have enacted any new medical waste management legislation, and/or reform any existing legislation, that has been prescribed in the updated National Health Care Waste Management Plan, to include but not be limited to, new or reformed policies, regulations, and standards pertaining hazardous waste management, occupational health and safety, infectious disease control, pollution prevention, and/or related subjects, per the recommendations of the updated plan.

The Government will have provided (1) the name and contact of the senior MoHSW official responsible for decentralization of health services to the district level, including liaison with MoLG and MOF; (2) the roles of MOHSW, the DHMT and hospitals and health centers (including CHAL)�in providing each of the 11 essential health services, and (3) a proposal for developing a professional DHMT/community health staff, including a proposed outline for career progressions for decentralized district staff, with a plan for consultations with and buy-in from nurses, health center and DHMT staff, and health sector management to be undertaken.

The Government will incorporate estimated capital and recurrent costs for implementation of a national medical waste management plan into the national budget, beginning with the 2008/2009 budget cycle based on cost estimates and finance plans available at that time, and accommodate updated costs annually thereafter.

The Government will, to the satisfaction of MCC, undertake a comprehensive technical review and update of the 2005 National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, including but not limited to preparation of updated capital and recurrent costs associated with the plan and a long-term finance strategy for funding these costs.

The MoHSW will have hired, to the satisfaction of MCC, a senior official with the relevant technical and managerial background to work within the Health Sector PIU, to manage all aspects of the medical waste management activity. Should the position become vacant, MCA-Lesotho will actively engage in the recruitment and selection of an individual to fill such vacancy.

Updated agreement between MoHSW and CHAL regarding infrastructure improvements in CHAL facilities. Such agreement will require CHAL facilities to maintain minimum service levels for a specified period or return equipment or refund MCA-Lesotho, unless otherwise agreed by MCC.
Vehicle management systems in place for each entity for which vehicles are to be procured.
